title: Clinton Foundation: Facts vs Claims
summary: Founded 1997; a public OPERATING foundation running its own programs (HIV/AIDS, climate, health). Ratings: Charity Navigator 4/4 stars; CharityWatch 'A' (~88% to mission). Documented controversies: foreign-government donations during her State tenure; disclosure lapses. Claims: 'Only 6% goes to charity' — DISPUTED (counts grants only, ignoring program expenses ~80–89%). 'Pay-to-play proven' — UNPROVEN; multiple inquiries, no charges.
tldr: Wikipedia's overview confirms the Foundation's top charity ratings — Charity Navigator's four of four stars and CharityWatch's 'A' (88% to mission) — while noting investigations through 2019 found no evidence of malfeasance.
ai_summary:
AI review of Wikipedia's Clinton Foundation overview, read in full:
- Ratings: Charity Navigator gave its highest rating, 'four out of four stars,' in 2016 after review of financial records and tax statements (it had briefly been on a watch list in 2015, removed December 2015). CharityWatch gave an 'A' rating for 2016, finding 88% of the foundation's money goes toward its charitable mission.
- Investigations: the Foundation was 'accused of wrongdoing, including a bribery and pay-to-play scheme, but multiple investigations through 2019 found no evidence of malfeasance.' Later probes (a Barr-era prosecutor; the Washington field office) are covered without resulting charges.
- Controversies documented: foreign-government donations during her State tenure and disclosure practices.
- Record summary verified accurate against the document.
